Figure_CMFA_controlled_evidence: Controlled evidence for CMFA on DSLR images. (a) Paired COCO AP differences between separately trained models with and without CMFA at seeds 0, 1, and 2. Open circles show individual-seed differences; diamonds and bars show the mean and sample SD. Mean gains are 0.498±0.145 points with AdamW and 0.513±0.091 with DualOpt. Only the CMFA configuration flag differs within each optimizer/seed pair; DualOpt here includes extra decay and rollback. (b) A seed-0 AdamW example changes an incorrect FDI 44 prediction to the reference 84. (c) For reference FDI 65, localization IoU increases from 0.553 to 0.894. Teal boxes denote ground truth, also shown dashed behind orange prediction boxes. Predictions use score≥0.30; one-to-one localization matching requires IoU≥0.50. The examples are illustrative and pertain to the stated controlled DSLR configurations. The seed bars describe validation training variability, not patient-level or independent-test uncertainty.
Figure_HOOA_controlled_evidence: Retrained HOOA branch controls on the Mobile validation cohort. (a) COCO AP, fixed-threshold F1, and raw-query duplicate-image rate for models trained without either branch, without high-pass, without second-order interaction, and with complete HOOA. Relative to neither branch, complete HOOA increases AP from 53.561 to 54.910 and F1 from 78.861% to 82.431%, while raw duplicate-image rate decreases from 43.182% to 27.273%. All four are single-seed retraining controls in the same reference configuration (prototype temperature 0.20); no seed uncertainty is assigned. Removing the second-order interaction retains the context branch in its place; removing high-pass supplies a zero branch. (b,c) Identical target crops show FDI 81 and 41, respectively, misclassified as 41 and 42 without either branch and correctly identified by the full module. Ground truth is teal and predictions orange; dashed teal boxes indicate the same ground truth in prediction panels. Score≥0.30 and one-to-one IoU≥0.50 matching are used. Duplicate-image rate is a raw-output diagnostic, not a clinical charting-error rate. Selected examples do not estimate correction frequencies.
Figure_Factor_supervision_evidence: Learning effects of the individual factor-supervision heads. (a) COCO AP with all three factor losses and after removing quadrant, within-quadrant position, or dentition supervision. Each control is independently trained at seed 0 with the same reference configuration and prototype temperature 0.20. Only the stated loss term is omitted; factor heads remain instantiated, and factor-score fusion is disabled during both training and inference. AP decreases by 0.654, 1.274, and 0.244 points, respectively. (b) Without quadrant supervision, the reference FDI 31 is predicted as 41. (c) Without position supervision, FDI 64 is predicted as 65. (d) Without dentition supervision, permanent FDI 33 is predicted as primary FDI 73. All-factor supervision yields the correct highest retained label in these examples. Teal denotes ground truth and orange predictions; dashed ground-truth boxes are repeated in prediction panels. Score≥0.30 and one-to-one IoU≥0.50 matching are used. Cases are illustrative; the AP result does not imply that every fixed-threshold metric improves or that statistical superiority has been established.
Figure_Factor_head_HiResCAM: Query-specific spatial attributions of the three factor heads from the representative DENT-STRIDE-Mobile seed-2 checkpoint (prototype temperature 0.50). Rows show reference FDI 64, 11, and 46; column headings give the actual predicted quadrant, position, and dentition. For each head, the scalar target is the correct factor logit minus its largest competing logit, evaluated for the highest-scoring correct-FDI query with localization IoU≥0.50 and score≥0.30. The attributed feature is the output of encoder.hooa_attention.0. The positive map is ReLU(sum_c A_c * d margin/d A_c), retaining spatial gradients (HiResCAM form). The actual gradient maps are computed over the full image without ground-truth masking; the shown oral crops are identical across heads. Each map is scaled by its full-image maximum to display relative spatial structure; color intensity is not comparable as an absolute effect across heads. Teal/white boxes locate the queried reference tooth and do not constrain the attribution. The native detached query-content initialization path is not traversed by these gradients; conditional input occlusion complements this partial-path explanation. These are post hoc gradient explanations, not native attention gates, a faithfulness guarantee for this Transformer architecture, or standalone evidence of a performance gain. The retrained supervision controls provide the performance evidence.

Figure_Factor_head_confusions: Factor-head classification on 2,339 uniquely localized ordinary queries from all 220 Mobile validation images using the representative seed-2 checkpoint (prototype temperature 0.50). Matrices are row-normalized percentages; quadrant, position, and dentition accuracies are 95.08%, 96.07%, and 95.55%, respectively. Gray rows have no reference observations. A query is eligible when its maximum sigmoid score is≥0.30; class-agnostic one-to-one localization matching requires IoU≥0.50. These conditional head accuracies are not detector recall or complete FDI detection accuracy; no calibration or clinical utility claim follows from them.
Figure_Factor_head_spatial_support: Spatial support of the individual factor-head decisions. Three Mobile examples use the representative seed-2 checkpoint with prototype temperature 0.50. The target FDI and each actual head prediction are shown above the images. Positive attributions are computed for the correct factor logit minus its strongest alternative at the HOOA level-0 output, using ReLU(sum_c activation_c times gradient_c). Red and amber mark the smallest sets of feature-grid cells accounting for at least 50% and 90% of the full-image positive attribution, respectively; the sets are nested and ties at a threshold are retained. Maps are computed over the full image, not masked by the ground-truth tooth. Dashed boxes only locate the queried reference tooth. This mass-support display makes sparse gradients visible without smoothing, painting anatomical regions, or interpreting them as native attention probabilities. Context outside the tooth can also contribute. These selected examples explain factor decisions; retrained supervision ablations, not the colors, provide evidence of detection benefit. The native detached query-content initialization path is not traversed by these gradients; conditional input occlusion complements this partial-path explanation.
Figure_Factor_head_occlusion_heatmaps: Conditional input-occlusion sensitivity of the factor heads. Rows show Mobile reference FDI 64, 11, and 46 using the same seed-2 checkpoint (prototype temperature 0.50). Each 1024×1024 input is perturbed at 841 sliding locations using a 128×128 patch with stride 32, filled with that image's RGB channel means. The scalar is the correct factor logit minus its strongest unoccluded alternative. Red indicates that occluding the region reduces the decision margin; blue indicates that it increases the margin. The dense signed map averages margin drops over all patches covering each pixel; no Gaussian smoothing or ground-truth spatial masking is applied. Each head has one common symmetric logit-margin scale across the three images. Encoder anchor selection and query order are fixed to the unoccluded pass, while query content and downstream predictions are recomputed for every perturbed input. This prevents query swaps and includes the query-content path detached in the gradient analysis. Unoccluded predictions are exactly unchanged by this conditioning. Dashed boxes locate the queried tooth; surrounding context can also influence the factor decisions. This is conditional-query sensitivity, not native attention, native detector accuracy on occluded images, or an independent proof of model efficacy. Mean-color masks may introduce artificial edges. Pure sensitivity maps are shown to avoid dilution by photographic colors.
